message.content:
Below is a concise list of the **long‑weekend holidays** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A “long weekend” is defined as a public holiday that creates a three‑day break (Friday‑Saturday‑Sunday or Saturday‑Sunday‑Monday).  

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Notes |
|-------------|---------|-------|
| **Jan 2** | New Year’s Day (observed) | New Year’s Day fell on Sunday Jan 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jan 2, giving a long weekend (Dec 30–Jan 2). |
| **Feb 20** | Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario, New Brunswick, Manitoba, Prince Edward Island) | Monday holiday – long weekend (Feb 18–20). |
| **Apr 7** | Good Friday | Friday holiday – long weekend (Apr 7–9). |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Monday holiday – long weekend (May 20–22). |
| **Jul 3** | Canada Day (observed) | Canada Day fell on Saturday Jul 1, so the holiday was observed on Monday Jul 3, giving a long weekend (Jul 1–3). |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Monday holiday – long weekend (Sep 2–4). |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Monday holiday – long weekend (Oct 7–9). |
| **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | Monday holiday – long weekend (Nov 9–11). |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Monday holiday – long weekend (Dec 23–25). |

> **Provinces with additional long‑weekend holidays**  
> Some provinces observe extra holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in British Columbia). Those are not listed here because they are not nationwide.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app. If you need province‑specific long weekends or a different format, just let me know!
